compliance_note: TCEC NNUE guideline: all training data generated by the engine's own search/evaluation. Positions from self-play with NNUE explicitly disabled (classical PST seed); labels from Luna's own search, not Stockfish. See probe log for the UseNNUE=false verification. NOTE on resolve_truncated_wdl.py: that script is compliant by inheritance, not by construction — it only consumes eval_cp already produced upstream (by annotate_positions_luna.py / annotate_incremental_gen1.py here), it never calls an engine itself. If the upstream annotator is ever swapped for a non-compliant one, this file becomes non-compliant with zero lines of its own changed. Its own compliance must be re-checked against whatever produces its input, not assumed from its own source.
self_play_eval_source: classical PST (UCI: setoption name UseNNUE value false)

normal_openings.filter_eval_source: Luna classical PST (UseNNUE=false, confirmed via probe before generating)

endgame_openings.trivial_draw_filter: no pawns AND no rooks/queens AND <=1 minor piece total (K+minor vs K, K vs K)
endgame_openings.note: FEN are real positions from played lichess games (via the public puzzle export); only used as starting-position pool, no evaluation/label taken from this source.

commit_mismatch_note: Self-play used engine commit b0cfb9378fad417bf03d6bf662d4738d7adadc66; labels were annotated with commit 076defcb93d4a1dc834d4ecd5132f45ba9a311d2. These differ because the quiescence check_time fix (076defc) landed after self-play for this shard had already run. The fix affects time/node budget enforcement inside quiescence search, not move legality or board state — positions extracted under the pre-fix commit remain valid. Only the label (this shard's evaluation/bestmove annotation) comes from the post-fix commit.
